steps.title: Find the client's documents (three routes, every try logged) and register each one
do: Find the documents the page below lists in the client's own folders. Try the routes IN THIS ORDER and record EVERY try, failures too:
1  device: the computer (local drive / OneDrive)    2  m365: the Microsoft 365 connector    3  zapier: the Zapier Office 365 tools
Record each try: python3 {scripts}/run.py access {run} --purpose locate --route device|m365|zapier --result failed|found --note "what you did"
Register each document you bring: python3 {scripts}/run.py doc {run} --role ROLE --file <local copy> --route <the route>   (ROLE is on the page below)

The RGAR report and the Fact Find Summary can never be missing. If there is no Fact Find Summary, STOP and ask Paul (never read the raw fillable Fact Find through a visual route instead). An older Fact Find Summary that does not exist: ask Paul, then python3 {scripts}/run.py doc {run} --missing fact_find_summary_older --said "Paul's words"

Show Paul the 'what I found' list (one line per document: file name, date, folder, and anything missing, conflicting or unreadable) in your reply. The program checks every file is readable and keeps its text so every figure you enter can be checked against it.
steps.proof: the tries are logged in order and the RGAR report and the Fact Find Summary are registered

steps.title: Read the RGAR report and the Fact Find Summary, one page at a time
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/run.py read {run}

The program shows the text page by page. Read each page fully, then acknowledge it with a one-line note (`run.py read {run} --ack ROLE:PAGE --note "..."`). Pages are acknowledged in order; a page with no readable text must be viewed as an image by you.
steps.proof: every page was served in order and acknowledged

steps.title: Enter the answers with their sources; the program checks every figure against the documents
do: Write ONE answers file in the layout the page below describes, every answer with its source, then run: python3 {scripts}/run.py answers {run} --file <your answers file>

The program refuses a figure, name, age, date of birth, employer, job title, income or email it cannot find in the right document's text, a net target that is not the figure after its label in the Fact Find Summary, an age that does not agree with the RGAR's date of birth, a lump sum or monthly amount of R 0, a conflict between sources (then STOP and ask Paul).

Ask Paul for what only he can give: the meetings already held (pre-filled from the file names) and the next meeting day, date and time. Never type a figure from memory and never copy one from another client.
steps.proof: the answers are valid, sourced, free of conflicts, and every figure was found in the right document's text

steps.title: Show Paul the confirmation table, ask ONE question, record his yes
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/run.py show {run}
Put the whole table it prints in your reply (it includes the email subject and the exact Teams message to Sitamah) and ask exactly the one question it gives. Nothing is built before his clear yes.
When he says yes, record his own words: python3 {scripts}/run.py approve {run} --said "his exact words"
If an answer changes, run answers and show again: the earlier yes then no longer counts.
steps.proof: Paul was shown exactly these answers and said yes

steps.title: The program fills the fixed template and builds the email, the saved copy and the text for the draft
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/run.py build {run}

It fills the template from your confirmed answers (never typed), computes every weekday, adds up the fee total, makes the full copy, the no-logo copy and the text for the Outlook draft, and checks them. You never edit a script, the template or the HTML.
Send the full copy (with the logo) to Paul in the chat with the exact file name the program gives.
steps.proof: the three files are exactly what the program builds from the confirmed answers and pass the program's checks

steps.title: Save the no-logo copy and a copy of the RGAR PDF in the RA transaction folder's Comparative Quotes, never overwriting without Paul's yes
do: List the client's RA transaction folder > `Comparative Quotes` (computer first, then Microsoft 365, then Zapier; record every try with --purpose save) and note the file names already there. Then: python3 {scripts}/run.py name {run} --existing "name one.html;name two.html"
If a file with the same name exists the program stops: ask Paul; only with his yes run it again with --overwrite-yes "his words".

Save exactly the file it names (the no-logo copy; never retype or truncate the logo). Then put a copy of the RGAR PDF in the same folder (`sharepoint_copy_item` with `destinationParentItemId`; the original stays where it is). List the folder again and record what it shows:

python3 {scripts}/run.py receipt {run} save.folder <the folder path>   save.listed_bytes <the html's size in the listing>   save.rgar_name <the RGAR file name in the listing>   save.rgar_listed_bytes <its size>
Tell Paul in plain words that the saved copy has no logo (the Outlook draft gets Paul's signature and logo separately).
steps.proof: the derived name was used, nothing was overwritten without Paul's yes, the folder is the RA transaction folder's Comparative Quotes, the listed size equals the local file and the RGAR copy is in the listing

steps.title: Make the Outlook draft with Claude in Chrome (never sent by Claude) and read it back for the program
do: Follow the page below. The text to paste is the draft_body.html the program built. Read the saved draft back, save the read-back to a file and run: python3 {scripts}/run.py draft {run} --file <the saved read-back>
Every line must be a green tick. Then record the cleanup: run.py receipt {run} draft.tab_closed yes   run.py receipt {run} draft.stray_deleted <number or none>
steps.proof: the saved read-back of the draft passes every program check and the cleanup is recorded

steps.title: Message Sitamah on Teams through Zapier (the wording is the program's) and read the posted message back
do: Look in the 1:1 chat for whether the same time-of-day greeting was already used today by Paul or Claude, then run: python3 {scripts}/run.py message {run} --used-today yes|no

Send exactly the message it prints, as it says. Read the posted message back, save it to a file, record the receipts it names and run: python3 {scripts}/run.py messagecheck {run} --file <the saved read-back>
steps.proof: the message went to the 1:1 chat as markdown and its read-back passes every program check

steps.title: The final check and the SHORT AUDIT for Paul
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/run.py done {run} final
Put in your reply, as it is: where the copy was saved, the draft's status, that Sitamah was messaged, then the short audit. Nothing longer.
Any red cross means the job is not finished: say so.
steps.proof: the final checker prints no red cross
